item.title: BLAST significance depends on the search space, not only sequence identity
item.content: BLAST significance is influenced by alignment score and search-space size. A match cannot be judged reliably from percent identity alone; alignment length, composition, gaps, score, and E-value provide necessary context.
item.explanationMarkdown:
A very short exact or near-exact match may occur frequently by chance, whereas a long high-scoring alignment can be compelling.

This is why interpreting BLAST solely as “highest percent identity wins” is unsafe. Biological interpretation should also consider coverage, alignment length, E-value, query/database context, and whether the matched region corresponds to the biology of interest.

cards.question: Which is the best reason not to rank BLAST hits using percent identity alone?
options: Percent identity is never reported by BLAST.
Statistical significance also depends on alignment score, length/search space, and other alignment properties.
E-values are independent of database size, so identity is redundant.
Only the alphabetical order of database accessions is statistically meaningful.
cards.explanation: Percent identity must be interpreted with alignment length/coverage, score, E-value, composition and search context.
